messages.author: deafb33e1fc42f73
messages.subject: Colouring points by multiple categories
parts:
I have a dataset with two metadata categories, Treatment and Timepoint.

I have a scatterplot of points and I can colour the points using "color = "Treatment"" or "colour = "Timepoint""

Is it possible to colour by both treatment _and_ timepoint so that every treatment/timepoint combination has its own colour? Right now I have a workaround with color for one category and shape for the other, but this will stop working once I have more than two categories.

Thanks!

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: Colouring points by multiple categories
parts:
On 14-06-30 11:00 AM, J. C. Szamosi wrote:
> I have a dataset with two metadata categories, Treatment and Timepoint.
>
> I have a scatterplot of points and I can colour the points using "color
> = "Treatment"" or "colour = "Timepoint""
>
> Is it possible to colour by both treatment _and_ timepoint so that every
> treatment/timepoint combination has its own colour? Right now I have a
> workaround with color for one category and shape for the other, but this
> will stop working once I have more than two categories.
>
> Thanks!

Probably the best way to do this is
colour=interaction(Treatment,Timepoint) [you may want to create the
interaction up front, as a new variable in your data set, rather than on
the fly].

It gets tricky if you want the colours to be related (e.g. red vs blue
for two times, light vs dark for two treatments) -- using
colour=Timepoint, alpha=Treatment can work, or you can make the
interaction and set up scale_colour_manual however you like.

messages.author: bcea08701fe87658
messages.subject: Re: Colouring points by multiple categories
parts:
Another possibility is to use:

scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Paired")

This palette contains a number of light-dark colour pairs. I'm not sure how you would go about choosing a specific pair though... I made a variable "sample", which enumerated each combination of "treatment" and "time-point" (2x2 in my case), and this function sensibly assigned colour pairs.

Cheers
